R134.note: In-process PowerShell with AddParameter closes the injection, but the response silently changes from powershell.exe's formatted stdout to joined PSObject.ToString() values, a new catch-all returns 400 with ex.Message, and the required Microsoft.PowerShell.SDK package is never mentioned.

R135.note: resolve then toRealPath with a Path.startsWith containment check against the real base rejects absolute, dotted and symlinked escapes before readAllBytes, and in-base reports still return their bytes.

R136.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) replaces the time-derived uniqid and drops the attacker-supplied prefix; token stays an opaque string stored and mailed the same way.

R137.note: Positional ? placeholder with the LIKE pattern bound as the parameter value is the correct ODBC shape; wildcard semantics of user-supplied % are unchanged from the original.

R138.note: html.EscapeString on both interpolated fields closes the sink; the local variable named html shadows the package after the declaration, which compiles and changes nothing but is untidy.

R139.note: Generic body replaces e.getMessage() with the same 400 status; server-side logging is suggested but not added, which is not harmful.

R140.note: EJS <%= %> escaping closes the XSS, but the write-up wrongly claims EJS ships with Express - it is a separate npm dependency, and without installing it res.render fails for every request; markup whitespace also changes.

R141.note: Adding @csrf_protect matches the sibling route and the case's stated fix; only defect is the docstring still saying the decorator is missing.

R142.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes into the same 16-byte buffer preserves the base64 response shape; the created RNG instance is not disposed, which is minor.

R143.note: Build fails: $this->authorize() is undefined because the controller does not extend the base Controller or use AuthorizesRequests, so authorized users hit a fatal error after the can middleware passes, and the write-up does not say so.

R144.note: Character allowlist blocks cmd metacharacters but the sink is still cmd /C with a concatenated string and a leading-dash value like -t still reaches ping as a flag (hangs CombinedOutput); the allowlist also rejects IPv6 targets containing colons that the original accepted.

R145.note: Allowlist dict is the right mechanism for import_module, but it silently rewrites module names to plugins.csv_export / plugins.pdf_export when the docstring says plugins are importable as csv_export, and drops any other installed plugin without saying so.

R146.note: jwt.verify with pinned algorithms and a try/catch closes the forged-token path; the env-sourced secret, HS256 assumption, new 500 on missing config and changed 401 message are all stated in the write-up.

R147.note: PreparedStatement with setString binds data as a value; result handling and cleanup are unchanged.

R148.note: Removing [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] lets the global AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter apply; the comment confirms the legacy client migration is finished so no legitimate caller is blocked.
